heading: CHAPTER VI.
title: CONCERNING NEW PRINCIPALITIES WHICH ARE ACQUIRED BY ONE'S OWN ARMS AND ABILITY
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Rich but tightly unified founding chapter.
The governing pressure is the difficulty of introducing a new order against entrenched enemies and lukewarm future beneficiaries.
Any reader-facing use of force should stay tied to the source's distinction between persuasion alone and enforceable power.
